assessment_title: Physical Sciences Grade 12 Term 3 Controlled Test
subject: Physical Sciences

sections.title: QUESTION 1: INTERNAL RESISTANCE
sections.instructions: Use Source 1. Show formulae, substitutions and units.

questions.question: Distinguish between the emf of a cell and its terminal potential difference.
memo: Emf is energy supplied per coulomb/open-circuit potential difference.
Terminal potential difference is energy transferred per coulomb in the external circuit and decreases under load.

questions.question: Identify the independent variable, the dependent variable and ONE controlled variable in this investigation.
memo: Independent: current, varied with the variable resistor.
Dependent: terminal voltage.
Controlled: same cell/temperature/circuit components.

questions.question: Describe the relationship between terminal voltage and current shown by the data.
memo: Terminal voltage decreases linearly as current increases.

questions.question: Use the data and V = emf - Ir to determine the emf and internal resistance of the cell.
memo: r = 0.50 ohm.
Using any point, emf = V + Ir = 1.50 V.

questions.question: Calculate the terminal voltage and the potential difference across the internal resistance when the current is 0.70 A.
memo: Vinternal = Ir = 0.35 V.

questions.question: Explain why the switch should be opened between readings.
memo: To limit heating/discharge of the cell, which would change internal resistance/emf and reduce validity.

sections.title: QUESTION 2: PHOTOELECTRIC EFFECT
sections.instructions: Use Source 2 and the supplied constant h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J.s.

questions.question: Define the work function of a metal.
memo: The minimum energy needed to remove an electron from the metal surface.

questions.question: Calculate the work function of the metal.
Calculate the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons when the frequency is 8.0 x 10^14 Hz.
State the effect of increasing light intensity when the frequency is above f0, and explain what happens when the frequency is below f0.
memo: Above f0, more electrons are emitted per second but KEmax is unchanged.
Below f0, no electrons are emitted regardless of intensity.

questions.question: State why the photoelectric effect supports the particle model of light.
memo: Energy is transferred in discrete photons with energy hf; one photon transfers energy to one electron.

questions.question: Identify the anode and the cathode.
memo: Anode: Zn; cathode: Cu.

questions.question: State the direction of electron flow in the external circuit.
memo: From the zinc electrode to the copper electrode.

questions.question: Write the oxidation and reduction half-reactions.
memo: Zn(s) -> Zn2+(aq) + 2e-.
Cu2+(aq) + 2e- -> Cu(s).

questions.question: Write the overall cell reaction.
memo: Zn(s) + Cu2+(aq) -> Zn2+(aq) + Cu(s).

questions.question: Calculate the standard emf of the cell and state whether the reaction is spontaneous.
memo: Positive Ecell means the reaction is spontaneous under standard conditions.

questions.question: Explain the function of the salt bridge.
memo: It permits ion movement, maintains electrical neutrality and completes the circuit without mixing the half-cell solutions directly.

questions.question: State how the cell potential changes as Zn2+ concentration increases and Cu2+ concentration decreases while the cell discharges.
memo: The cell potential decreases and approaches zero at equilibrium.
